liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (4 reviews): Scarlet>Fire is called one of the best ever, ranked alongside the Cornell version; Scarlet/Fire closes set one with a very spacey coda [6][10][11][15]
- **Jack A Roe** (2 reviews): This Jack A Roe, with strong bass licks, was released on Phil's 2CD set in the late 1990s; Phil Zone rightly chose this as a definitive Jack-a-roe [7][15]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Half Step they've heard, with a lovely transition into El Paso [7]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Described as nearly flawless [10]
- **Big River** (1 review): Big River has a funky back-beat, like Phil describes for Jack A Roe in his Phil Zone notes [13]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer heard little improvisation at the end of Fire [11]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Reviewer says Samson crackles with electricity [6]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Terrapin among the best ever [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-17.121485.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 215 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd77-05-17.sbd.weiner.18554.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 194 min; rated 4.68/5 by 79 [3]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.leonard.1107.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.58/5 by 12 [4]. Said about its sound: Tuning pauses were shortened in some places, and the Sugar Magnolia encore is missing [4]
- **gd1977-05-17.aud.maizner.minches.88771.flac16**: audience recording; 25 songs; 216 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended Alabama and knows older fans who were actually at this Tuscaloosa show [16]
- Reviewer says this show is worth owning along with 5/19/77 [7]
- Reviewer sees the show as a warmup for the remarkable run of shows that followed [10]
- Reviewer says it rivals 5/8/77 without surpassing it [14]
- Reviewer says the two weeks from Barton Hall to here rival Europe 1972, with a more seasoned band [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-17.121485.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by matrix by dusborne; source: 2 source matrix: Soundboard (shnid=18554): SBDMR > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN and Aud (shnid=88771): Recording by Steve Maizner: Sony ECM-990s>Sony TC153; Transfer… [1]. Also: Steve Maizner recorded the show from the audience; David Minches worked on and transferred the audience tape; This matrix combines Noah Weiner's soundboard work with the audience recording [1]
- **gd77-05-17.sbd.weiner.18554.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [3]. Also: Reviewer long had this Scarlet-Fire on a tape labeled Eugene '78 space, and searched since 1982 for its true source [12]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.leonard.1107.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Brian Leopard; source: SBD>MR 7" (Baked)>DAT>Cass>DAT>CD [4]. Also: Uploader ripped it with EAC from a disc received from Andy Singer [4]
- **gd1977-05-17.aud.maizner.minches.88771.flac16**: taped by Steve Maizner; transferred by David Minches; source: Sony ECM-990s>Sony TC153 [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Patrick D. Covert: [Grateful Dead Tuscaloosa AL 1977 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1295788/Grateful-Dead-Tuscaloosa-AL-1977-Concert-Poster) [19]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 5/17/77 Memorial Coliseum - Uni…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304785971/) [20]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304785971/) [21]
